payload.title: p2p-http join creates local membership only — relay's shared store not updated
MCP-created campfires not visible to p2p-http transport on other instances

payload.context: Repro: daemon joins via cf join --via <relay>/api <campfire-id>. Join succeeds (local CBOR written), but cf send gets: 'delivery to peer 0 failed: not a campfire member'. Root cause: cfhttp.Join only writes to the daemon's local store (SQLite). The relay's Azure Table Storage peer_endpoints table is never updated. The relay's authMiddleware checks that table, so it rejects subsequent deliver requests from the daemon. Fix: relay handleJoin must write new member to shared Azure Table Storage peer_endpoints.

Repro: create campfire via MCP (campfire_create), then cf join --via <relay>/api <campfire-id> from a different process. Returns 404 'campfire not found on this server'. Root cause: cf-mcp stores MCP-created campfires in per-instance SQLite only. When join request routes to a different Azure Functions instance, that instance has no record. Fix: campfire_create must write to shared Azure Table Storage. Confirmed: campfires created and joined on same instance burst work fine.

payload.context:
## Outcome
campfire_discover (MCP tool) returns beacons from campfires created on ANY Azure Functions instance, not just the current one.

## Root cause
beacon.Publish writes JSON files to s.beaconDir (local filesystem). beacon.Scan reads them back. Other instances have empty beacon dirs.

## Fix
When publishing a beacon (main.go:1456, 1579, 3244), also write the beacon data to the global store. When scanning (main.go:2000, 2977), also query the global store. The global store already has a non-namespaced TableStore on TransportRouter — add a beacon storage method.

Option: store beacons as messages in the global store with a well-known tag (e.g. "beacon:<campfireID>"), or add a dedicated beacons table to aztable.

## Files
- cmd/cf-mcp/main.go — handleCreateHTTP (1579), handleCreate (1456), handleDM (3244), handleDiscover (2000), handleJoin beacon resolution (2977)
- pkg/store/aztable/aztable.go — may need a beacon table or use existing message table
- pkg/beacon/ — Publish/Scan interface

## Done condition
Create campfire on instance A via campfire_create. On instance B, campfire_discover returns the beacon. Test: create campfire, verify beacon exists in aztable, verify Scan against aztable returns it.

## Constraints
- Do not change the beacon.Beacon struct or local filesystem beacon format
- Local beacons still work for non-hosted mode (no Azure)

## Outcome
When a session joins a remote campfire via handleRemoteJoin (MCP campfire_join with peer_endpoint), the campfire is accessible for p2p-http on any instance — not just the one that joined.

## Root cause
handleRemoteJoin (main.go:2030) writes campfire state to local filesystem (campfire.cbor), records membership in session store, and registers with TransportRouter.RegisterForSession — all per-instance. The global store is never written to.

## Fix
After the existing RegisterForSession call (main.go:2167-2168), write to TransportRouter.GlobalStore() — same pattern as handleCreateHTTP:
1. gs.AddMembership with CampfirePrivKey (the campfire private key is in cfState from cfhttp.Join result)
2. gs.UpsertPeerEndpoint for the creator and any peers from the join result
3. gs.UpsertPeerEndpoint for self (the server) so checkMembership passes

## Files
- cmd/cf-mcp/main.go — handleRemoteJoin (~line 2030-2170)
- cmd/cf-mcp/transport_http.go — GlobalStore() already exists

## Done condition
Session A joins a remote campfire via campfire_join. External CLI agent does cf join --via <relay>/api <id> — request hits instance B. Join succeeds (not 404). Then CLI agent sends a message — delivery succeeds (not 403).

## Constraints
- Only write to global store in HTTP mode (s.httpTransport != nil)
- SSRF validation on peer endpoints must still apply

## Outcome
Per-session HTTP transports reconstructed on a different instance can sign provenance hops and serve join requests — without local campfire.cbor files.

## Root cause
session.go:851-857 — the KeyProvider closure reads from fsT.ReadState(campfireID) which uses the local filesystem. On instance B, the CBOR files don't exist.

## Fix
Change the KeyProvider closure in getOrCreate (session.go:851-857) to first try the local filesystem (fast path for same-instance), then fall back to the global store's CampfirePrivKey field. The global store is available via the TransportRouter — pass it through SessionManager.

Approach:
1. Add a globalStore field to SessionManager (set during startup alongside storeFactory)
2. In getOrCreate, the KeyProvider closure: try fsT.ReadState first; if err, check globalStore.GetMembership(campfireID).CampfirePrivKey
3. Same for DeliveryModesProvider — fall back to default pull+push if local CBOR missing

## Files
- cmd/cf-mcp/session.go — getOrCreate (~line 845-868), SessionManager struct
- cmd/cf-mcp/main.go — wire globalStore on SessionManager at startup

## Done condition
Create campfire on instance A. Instance A's session is reaped. New session on instance B for the same operator — campfire_send works (KeyProvider finds the key from global store, not local CBOR).

## Constraints
- Local filesystem is still the fast path — don't remove it
- Depends on campfire-c13 (remote join global store) being done first so CampfirePrivKey is in global store

## Artifact type: code
## Test depth: feature
## Model tier: sonnet

## Outcome
Per-IP campfire_init rate limit counts across all instances, not per-instance.

## Root cause
session.go:427 — initRateLimiter holds map[string][]time.Time in memory. N instances = N× the intended limit.

## Fix
Replace the in-memory sliding window with an Azure Table Storage counter. Use a dedicated table or a row in the existing CampfireCounters table. The counter should track (IP, timestamp) with a TTL window.

Approach:
1. Add a RateLimitStore interface: Allow(ip string) bool
2. Implement with aztable: use CAS (ETag) to atomically increment a counter per IP with TTL window
3. Fall back to in-memory initRateLimiter when aztable is not configured (local dev)
4. Wire in SessionManager.checkInitRateLimit

## Files
- cmd/cf-mcp/session.go — initRateLimiter struct, checkInitRateLimit
- pkg/store/aztable/ — new rate limit table or extension

## Done condition
Configure rate limit to 3/min. Send 3 campfire_init requests from same IP to instance A — all succeed. Send 4th to instance B — rejected (rate limit exceeded). Verify counter is in Azure Table Storage.

## Constraints
- Must not add >50ms latency to campfire_init (Azure Table Storage point reads are ~10ms)
- Fall back to in-memory for non-hosted mode

## Test depth: feature
## Model tier: sonnet

## Outcome
Convention server registrations are refreshed from Azure Table Storage periodically so new registrations on other instances become visible.

## Root cause
convention_dispatch.go:27 — conventionServerLoadedCampfires is a sync.Map with no TTL. Once loaded, never refreshed. New server registrations from other instances are invisible.

## Fix
Add a TTL to the loaded flag. Instead of storing true, store the load timestamp. In loadConventionServersForCampfire, if the timestamp is older than a threshold (e.g. 5 minutes), reload from Azure Table Storage.

## Files
- cmd/cf-mcp/convention_dispatch.go — conventionServerLoadedCampfires, loadConventionServersForCampfire

## Done condition
Register convention server for campfire X on instance A. Instance B dispatches a message to campfire X — convention handler is loaded from aztable and dispatch succeeds (within 5 min TTL).

## Constraints
- Keep the sync.Map for fast-path (no lock contention)
- Only reload from aztable, not every check

## Artifact type: code
## Test depth: refactor
## Model tier: haiku

## Outcome
Audit entries have globally monotonic sequence numbers (or at least non-conflicting per-instance sequences).

## Root cause
audit.go:62 — AuditWriter holds an in-memory sequence counter. Two instances produce overlapping sequences.

## Fix
Use an Azure Table Storage atomic counter for the sequence. Or switch to UUID-based message IDs (which are already globally unique via campfire message IDs) and drop the sequence counter entirely.

Preferred approach: Drop the in-memory sequence counter. Use the campfire message timestamp (nanosecond precision) as the ordering field. The Merkle tree can use message IDs instead of sequence numbers.

## Files
- cmd/cf-mcp/audit.go — AuditWriter struct, AuditEntry struct, Log method

## Done condition
Two instances both write audit entries for the same campfire. Entries are ordered by timestamp. No sequence number conflicts. Merkle tree (if kept) uses message IDs.

## Constraints
- Audit entries must still be verifiable (signed, ordered)
- Don't break the audit campfire format for existing entries

payload.title: Convention adoption UX — send validation, install, adopt

payload.context:
## Outcome
When a user runs `cf send <id> --tag convention:operation '<json>'`, the send command validates the payload via `convention.Lint()` before posting. Invalid declarations fail with clear error messages showing parse failures. Valid declarations with warnings print warnings to stderr and proceed.

## Done condition
1. `cf send <id> --tag convention:operation '{"convention":"test"}'` fails with error naming missing fields (version, operation, signing)
2. A valid declaration payload sends successfully
3. A declaration with warnings (e.g., deprecated PayloadRequired field) prints warning to stderr but sends
4. Non-convention messages (no convention:operation tag) are unaffected — no validation
5. Tests prove all four behaviors

## Design reference
Conversation context. The gap: convention.ListOperations (pkg/convention/toolgen.go:206-208) silently skips Parse() failures. Users get no feedback when their declaration is malformed.

## Files to modify
- cmd/cf/cmd/send.go — Add lint check after building tags (line ~76), before protocol.Client.Send() (line ~99)
  - Check if tags contain convention.ConventionOperationTag
  - If so, call convention.Lint([]byte(payload))
  - If lint errors: return formatted error (reuse printLintResult pattern from convention_lint.go:63-81)
  - If lint warnings: print to stderr, continue
- cmd/cf/cmd/send_test.go — New or extended test file

## Files to read (reference)
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_lint.go — printLintResult() pattern (line 63-81), readDeclarationInput() (line 84-89)
- pkg/convention/lint.go — Lint() function (line 38-87), LintResult struct (line 25-29)
- pkg/convention/parser.go — ConventionOperationTag constant (line 174)
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_dispatch_test.go — setupDispatchEnv() for test campfire setup pattern

## Test depth
feature — new validation behavior on existing command

## Constraints
- Do NOT validate payloads for any tag other than convention:operation
- Do NOT change the Lint() function itself
- Do NOT block sends on warnings — only errors
- Keep the validation inline in send.go — do not extract to a helper (YAGNI, single use)

## Agent type
implementer

## Artifact type
code

payload.context:
## Outcome
\`cf convention install <campfire-id> <file.json>\` reads a declaration file, lints it, and posts it to the specified campfire as a properly-formatted convention:operation message. After installation, \`cf <campfire-id> help\` shows the new operation and \`cf <campfire-id> <operation> --help\` shows its args.

Also supports: \`cf convention install <campfire-id> --from <source-campfire-id>\` to copy all convention declarations from one campfire to another.

## Done condition
1. \`cf convention install <campfire-id> test-decl.json\` posts the declaration and \`cf <campfire-id> help\` lists the operation
2. Invalid declaration file (missing required fields) fails with lint errors before posting
3. \`cf convention install <campfire-id> --from <source-campfire>\` copies all declarations from source
4. Duplicate detection: installing the same declaration twice skips the duplicate (compare convention+operation+version)
5. Directory support: \`cf convention install <campfire-id> ./decls/\` installs all .json files in directory
6. Tests prove all behaviors

## Design reference
Conversation context. The gap: seed path (cmd/cf/cmd/seed.go) only works at campfire creation time. No way to add conventions to existing campfires.

## Files to create
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_install.go — New cobra subcommand of conventionCmd

## Files to read (reference)
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_promote.go — promoteSingle() pattern: lint → parse → conflict check → send (lines 122-168). Use same pattern. sendDeclarationViaTransport() (line 170+) for the post mechanism.
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_lint.go — readDeclarationsFromPath() (line 91-123) for reading files/directories. declSource struct (line 126-129).
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_dispatch.go — listConventionOperations() to read existing declarations for duplicate detection
- cmd/cf/cmd/send.go — protocol.New(s, agentID) and client.Send() pattern (lines 98-106)
- pkg/convention/parser.go — Parse() for extracting convention+operation+version
- pkg/convention/toolgen.go — ConventionOperationTag constant

## Implementation sketch
1. Register \`conventionInstallCmd\` as subcommand of \`conventionCmd\`
2. Args: campfire-id (required positional), file/dir (optional positional), --from flag (optional)
3. If --from: read declarations from source campfire via listConventionOperations(), then post each to target
4. If file/dir: use readDeclarationsFromPath() to read payloads
5. For each payload: Lint() → if errors, print and skip. Parse() to extract key. Check existing declarations on target for duplicates. Send via protocol.Client.Send() with convention:operation tag.
6. Print summary: N installed, N skipped (duplicate), N failed (lint)

## Test depth
feature — new CLI command

## Test file
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_install_test.go — Use setupDispatchEnv() pattern from convention_dispatch_test.go. Test: install from file, install from directory, install with --from, duplicate skip, lint failure.

## Constraints
- Reuse existing helpers: readDeclarationsFromPath(), convention.Lint(), protocol.Client.Send()
- Do NOT create a new transport mechanism — use protocol.Client.Send() which handles transport dispatch
- Do NOT modify convention.go beyond adding the subcommand registration
- Follow the promote command pattern for validation pipeline

## Agent type
implementer

## Artifact type
code

payload.context:
## Outcome
\`cf convention adopt <file.json>\` lints a declaration, posts it to the ~home campfire as a convention:operation message, and prints confirmation with the trust fingerprint. After adoption, \`cf trust show\` lists the convention under "Adopted conventions" with source "seed" (because loadLocalPolicyEngine reads ~home declarations via SeedConventions).

Also supports: \`cf convention adopt --from <campfire-id>\` to adopt all conventions from a campfire (copies their declarations to ~home).

## Done condition
1. \`cf convention adopt test-decl.json\` posts to ~home and \`cf trust show\` lists the convention
2. Invalid declaration file fails with lint errors
3. \`cf convention adopt --from <campfire-id>\` copies all declarations from source campfire to ~home
4. Duplicate detection: adopting the same declaration twice skips the duplicate
5. After adoption, creating a new campfire with \`cf create\` AND a seed beacon pointing to ~home seeds the convention (verify: the convention appears in \`cf <new-campfire> help\`)
6. Tests prove behaviors 1-4 (behavior 5 is integration-level, tested in e2e verification)

## Design reference
Conversation context. The gap: trust.PolicyEngine.Adopt() exists (pkg/trust/policy.go:152-170) but has no CLI surface. loadLocalPolicyEngine() (cmd/cf/cmd/trust.go:48-62) reads from ~home and calls SeedConventions(). Posting to ~home is the persistence mechanism.

## Files to create
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_adopt.go — New cobra subcommand of conventionCmd

## Files to read (reference)
- cmd/cf/cmd/trust.go — loadLocalPolicyEngine() (line 48-62) to understand how ~home → trust policy works
- cmd/cf/cmd/trust_show.go — how adopted conventions are displayed
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_lint.go — readDeclarationsFromPath(), readDeclarationInput() for reading files
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_install.go — (created in parallel item) same pattern but different target campfire
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_promote.go — promoteSingle() pattern for lint → parse → post
- pkg/trust/policy.go — AdoptedConvention struct (line 50-58), SemanticFingerprint for display
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_dispatch.go — listConventionOperations() for reading existing declarations

## Implementation sketch
1. Register \`conventionAdoptCmd\` as subcommand of \`conventionCmd\`
2. Args: file/dir (optional positional), --from flag (optional)
3. Resolve ~home campfire via resolveCampfireID("~home", s) — if ~home doesn't exist, error: "no ~home campfire — run cf init first"
4. If --from: read declarations from source campfire, post each to ~home
5. If file/dir: read payloads, lint each, post to ~home
6. For each: lint → check existing on ~home for duplicates → post with convention:operation tag
7. Print confirmation with convention name, operation, version, and fingerprint (from trust.SemanticFingerprint)
8. Print: "Adopted N conventions. Run 'cf trust show' to verify."

## Test depth
feature — new CLI command

## Test file
- cmd/cf/cmd/convention_adopt_test.go — Setup: create identity and store with ~home campfire. Test: adopt from file, adopt with --from, duplicate skip, lint failure, trust show reflects adoption.

## Constraints
- Persistence is through ~home campfire messages — do NOT write to a separate file or database
- Do NOT modify trust.go or the PolicyEngine — the existing loadLocalPolicyEngine() mechanism handles reading
- Do NOT modify convention.go beyond adding the subcommand registration
- Reuse readDeclarationsFromPath(), convention.Lint(), protocol.Client.Send()

implementer

payload.context:
## Role
Veracity adversary — run concurrently with Wave 1 implementers. Read their tests as they land. Challenge any done condition that can be satisfied by mocking the primary interface.

## Scope
Three implementation items in Wave 1:
- campfire-1a7: cf send validates convention:operation payloads before posting
- campfire-098: cf convention install posts validated declarations to existing campfires
- campfire-672: cf convention adopt registers declarations in local trust policy via ~home

## What to verify
For each implementation item:
1. Does the test actually call convention.Lint() with a real payload (not a mock)?
2. Does the test post a real message to a real (test) campfire store (not a mock)?
3. Does the test verify the message appears in the store via ListMessages (not just checking return value)?
4. For send validation: does the test prove that an invalid payload is REJECTED (not just that valid payloads succeed)?
5. For install: does the test prove that cf <campfire> help shows the installed operation (end-to-end, not just message posted)?
6. For adopt: does the test prove that loadLocalPolicyEngine() returns the adopted convention (not just message posted)?
